title: Software Development Engineer - 2
jobDescription:
Sat Sure is a global Earth intelligence company headquartered in India. Founded in 2017, Sat Sure owns the full Earth observation data value chain
- from the upstream payload infrastructure to the foundational deep-tech and AI layers, to the downstream decision intelligence solutions. We work with private companies and government bodies across Agri-tech, Agri-banking, forestry, critical infrastructure, and aviation. Through our subsidiary Kaleid EO, Sat Sure is building multispectral payloads for high-definition space imagery with edge computing capabilities, powering both sovereign and commercial applications.

ROLE:
As a Software Development Engineer 2, you will design, build, and operate full-stack software that powers Sat Sure's geospatial products. You will own features and services end-to-end from React frontends to Fast API services to Postgre SQL data layers running on AWS
- and work closely with cross-functional teams, including product managers, data engineers, geospatial analysts, and other software engineers, to ship reliable software that runs at scale in production. Key

RESPONSIBILITIES:
Feature Ownership: Take features from design through deployment and support
- scoping the work, breaking it down, and shipping it with minimal hand-holding. Full-Stack Development: Build responsive React frontends, robust Fast API backend services, and well-modelled Postgre SQL data layers, delivering cohesive, maintainable code that enhances the user experience. Backend & API Engineering: Write clean, well-documented REST/async APIs in Fast API, applying established patterns for authentication/authorization, pagination, validation, and error handling. Frontend Engineering: Develop modular, reusable React components (state management, routing, code-splitting), working with product and design to translate requirements into intuitive interfaces. Data Layer & Persistence: Write and tune schemas, indexes, and queries in Postgre SQL (including geospatial workloads via Post GIS) for correctness and good performance under real traffic. Cloud & Infrastructure: Deploy and run services on AWS using managed services, containers, and infrastructure-as-code, with attention to cost, security, and observability. Performance & Debugging: Investigate and fix bottlenecks across the stack
- frontend rendering, API latency, slow queries, caching
- using profiling, indexing, and query optimisation. Quality & Reliability: Write automated tests, work within CI/CD pipelines, add meaningful monitoring and alerting, and participate in on-call and incident follow-ups for the services you own. Design Participation: Contribute to design discussions and technical proposals, participate in sprint planning, retrospectives, and design reviews, and communicate progress and trade-offs clearly. Peer Support: Give constructive code reviews, help onboard new joiners, and share what you learn with the team. Collaboration & Communication: Work with product and cross-functional teams to understand requirements and translate them into technical solutions, communicating effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Must-have: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science or a related field. 3-6 years of software development experience, with services you have shipped and supported in production. Experience building and operating web applications at scale , with an understanding of availability, latency, and failure handling. Solid full-stack engineering skills across React (frontend), Fast API / Python (backend), and Postgre SQL (data layer). Hands-on experience building applications on AWS (compute, storage, networking, managed databases, containers). Working knowledge of API design, relational databases, caching, and asynchronous patterns. Good fundamentals in data structures, algorithms, testing, CI/CD, and observability. Familiarity with Scrum or Agile frameworks such as Kanban. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, and the ability to work through ambiguity with support from the team. Good-to-have: Exposure to GIS / geospatial development
- Post GIS and spatial queries, geospatial formats/standards (Geo JSON, Shapefile, KML, Geo Parquet, STAC), and libraries such as GDAL, Rasterio, Geo Pandas, Shapely. Familiarity with mapping/visualisation libraries (Mapbox, Map Libre, Leaflet). Exposure to data engineering tooling such as Apache Airflow or Apache Spark, and lakehouse formats like Apache Iceberg. Experience with containers, Kubernetes, or Terraform. Interest or early experience in building AI / LLM-powered applications
- RAG, tool/function calling, prompt engineering, or agentic workflows. The role of a Software Development Engineer 2 is key to building and scaling the platforms that turn earth observation data into accessible insights across applications including agriculture, infrastructure, climate action, urban planning, and environmental monitoring. Benefits: Medical health cover for you and your family, including unlimited online doctor consultations Access to mental health experts for you and your family Dedicated allowances for learning and skill development Comprehensive leave policy with casual leaves, paid leaves, marriage leaves, bereavement leaves Interview Process: Intro call Assessment Interview rounds (2-3 rounds) Culture Round / HR round

title: Machine Learning Engineer - 2
jobDescription:
Sat Sure is a global Earth intelligence company headquartered in India. Founded in 2017, Sat Sure owns the full Earth observation data value chain
- from the upstream payload infrastructure to the foundational deep-tech and AI layers, to the downstream decision intelligence solutions. We work with private companies and government bodies across Agri-tech, Agri-banking, forestry, critical infrastructure, and aviation. Through our subsidiary Kaleid EO, Sat Sure is building multispectral payloads for high-definition space imagery with edge computing capabilities, powering both sovereign and commercial applications.

ROLE:
We are looking for a Machine Learning Engineer II to own a model workstream end-to-end
- not a single model, but the family of models behind a product line, and the decisions that keep them accurate, fast, and affordable in production. You will be handed goals and ideas, not finished solutions: you decide how to run the experiments to test them, own the optimization and serving strategy, and defend your choices with benchmarks and clear findings. This is a hands-on role. You will still write the training loop and read the Triton logs.

RESPONSIBILITIES:
Experiment Execution & Reporting: Own how a workstream's ideas get tested. Take the team's modelling proposals, turn them into well-run, reproducible training/fine-tuning experiments, monitor them, and report rigorous findings that decide what ships. You make pragmatic implementation choices; the research direction comes from Data Science. Model Optimization: Own the accuracy/latency/cost tradeoff for your models in production. Drive quantization (INT8/FP16), pruning, distillation, and ONNX/Tensor RT export; profile GPU utilization and eliminate the bottleneck rather than guessing at it. Pipelines at Scale: Design ML pipelines that survive real data
- petabyte-scale satellite archives, missing tiles, sensor drift, inconsistent projections. Make them reproducible and cheap to re-run. Productionization: Prepare models for production and support their deployment on KServe / Triton alongside the Platform team. You should understand how modern serving frameworks work and what they demand of a model
- batch sizing, concurrency, autoscaling behaviour, and failure modes under load
- and hand over artifacts that account for them. Evaluation & Benchmarking: Define what "good" means before training starts
- offline metrics, production SLOs, and the acceptance criteria a model must meet to ship. Monitoring & Drift: Own post-deployment model health. Instrument for drift, set thresholds, and drive the retraining decision rather than waiting to be told. Technical Mentorship: Review code, models, and experiment design from MLEs/Data Scientists. Raise the floor of the team's engineering practice. Qualification: 4-7 years of relevant experience as a Machine Learning Engineer or in an applied research/engineering role. Mandatory: Deep hands-on Py Torch expertise
- custom datasets, distributed/multi-GPU training, mixed precision, and inference optimization. You can read a Py Torch profiler trace and act on it. Mandatory: Multiple models shipped to production and kept in production, with evidence of measured latency/throughput improvements. Mandatory: Hands-on experience training, fine-tuning, debugging, optimizing, and productionizing modern deep-learning architectures, including CNNs, vision transformers, and vision foundation models such as DINO- and SAM-style models. You are comfortable reading unfamiliar model implementations, adapting them to new use cases, and improving their training efficiency, inference performance, and production reliability. Mandatory: Experience running experiments to a defined hypothesis with minimal supervision
- and reporting findings others could act on. Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, IT, Statistics, or a related field; non-IT degrees with strong relevant experience are acceptable. Must-have skills: ML Engineering Depth : You have debugged the training instability, found the data leak, and traced the production regression back to a preprocessing change. You know where models break in the real world. Training at Scale: Confident running distributed / multi-GPU training and fine-tuning jobs efficiently and reproducibly, and instrumenting them so the findings are trustworthy. Optimization Fluency : Quantization, distillation, ONNX/Tensor RT, and batching/concurrency tuning at the serving layer. You can quantify what each technique bought you. Feature & Data Pipelines: Scalable pipelines over raster/vector geospatial formats; comfortable with Rasterio/GDAL, tiling strategies, and the failure modes of remote sensing data. Python & Engineering Practice : Clean, tested, maintainable code. You write ML code other engineers can pick up. Containerization & Cloud: Confident with Docker and AWS (S3, EC2, ECR); you can reason about GPU instance selection and the cost of your own training runs. Serving Infrastructure: Familiarity with KServe, Triton, or an equivalent model-serving stack
- enough to understand how your model will be served and to work effectively with the team that runs it. Experimentation & Versioning : MLflow (or equivalent) used properly
- reproducible experiments, a model registry others can trust, and lineage from data to deployed artifact. Kubernetes (User Level): Submitting GPU jobs, reading pod logs, reasoning about resource requests and limits. Good-to-have: Background in geospatial or remote sensing ML (satellite imagery, SAR, multispectral, time-series of Earth observation data). Kernel-level bottleneck analysis and the ability to quantify what it bought you. CI/CD for ML
- automated training triggers, evaluation gates, and progressive rollout of models. CUDA-level debugging and custom kernel awareness. Experience with distributed training frameworks and large-scale data loading optimization. Exposure to cost optimization for GPU workloads (spot strategy, right-sizing, inference cost per prediction). Competencies: Ownership: You own the outcome, not the artifact. If the model is slow in production, you drive the diagnosis and the fix with whoever owns the infrastructure it runs on. Judgement: You know how to run an idea cheaply enough to get a signal fast, and when a negative result is conclusive. You do not over-engineer. Scientific Rigor: Hypothesis-driven experimentation with results others can reproduce from your tracking and write-ups alone. Collaboration & Influence: You can explain a tradeoff to a Data Scientist, a Platform engineer, and a domain expert
- and get all three to agree on a path. Mentorship: You make the engineers around you better through review, pairing, and clear technical writing. Interview Process: Intro call Take-home assessment (focus on model training, optimization & deployment) Interview rounds (ideally up to 3 rounds, including a deep dive on a model you have shipped and an ML system design discussion) Culture round / HR round

title: AI Product Lead
jobDescription:
About Sat Sure Sat Sure builds decision intelligence systems using artificial intelligence, large-scale data platforms, and complex real-world datasets. We are working on Dhaarini , an internal AI initiative focused on creating reusable capabilities from multimodal and temporal data. Dhaarini is not a single model or a standalone application. It is intended to support capabilities such as reusable representations, multimodal retrieval, temporal understanding and AI services that can be used across Sat Sure's platform and products. Role We are looking for an AI Product Lead to help structure and drive Dhaarini's AI capability development. You will work directly with the CTO and collaborate with AI scientists, ML engineers, platform teams and product managers. The role is suited to someone who understands AI development well enough to frame the right problems, define clear success criteria and help move useful experiments toward reusable product capabilities. You are not expected to be the deepest researcher or system architect. You will, however, need to be comfortable working with technical teams, asking difficult questions, and bringing product clarity to an area where the answers may not always be obvious. This is an individual-contributor role with cross-functional responsibility.

RESPONSIBILITIES:
Shape the AI capability roadmap Work with the CTO and AI leaders to define and prioritise Dhaarini's AI capabilities. Translate broad technical ideas into clear problem statements and capability requirements. Balance longer-term capability development with near-term validation. Support build, adapt or use-existing decisions based on evidence and feasibility. Structure experimentation and evaluation Convert ideas into clear hypotheses, experiments and decision points. Work with technical teams to define baselines, evaluation criteria and success measures. Ensure experiments answer meaningful technical or product questions. Capture learnings and support decisions on whether work should progress, change direction or stop. Support capability productisation Identify when a capability is ready to move beyond experimentation. Define its intended usage and product requirements. Work with platform and engineering teams to move validated capabilities toward integration. Reduce the number of useful experiments that remain limited to notebooks, demos or isolated implementations. Drive cross-functional execution Keep AI, platform and product teams aligned on shared priorities. Identify dependencies, risks and unresolved decisions early. Run reviews focused on evidence, learnings and next steps. Escalate important trade-offs with clear context and recommendations. What success looks like Within the first 6-12 months, you should have: Established a clear Dhaarini AI capability roadmap. Introduced a consistent way to frame and evaluate experiments. Helped validate two or more important technical hypotheses. Moved at least one reusable capability toward platform integration. Created a clear adoption path for at least one capability. Reduced repetitive or disconnected experimentation across teams. Experience: 5-7 years of experience across AI products, ML products, data products, technical product management, or applied AI. Must have: Experience working directly with AI/ML, data science or engineering teams. At least one example of taking an AI or data capability from problem definition toward production or operational use. Practical understanding of the AI lifecycle, including data, experimentation, evaluation, deployment, and monitoring. Ability to turn ambiguous technical ideas into clear priorities, requirements, and decisions. Strong product judgement and cross-functional execution skills. Ability to understand technical discussions and challenge assumptions constructively. Strong written and verbal communication. High ownership and comfort working in an evolving, zero-to-one environment. We are looking for someone who has worked directly with the AI product lifecycle, not only integrated third-party AI services into conventional software products. Good to have: Experience with computer vision, multimodal AI, embeddings or retrieval systems. Experience with MLOps, AI platforms or large-scale data systems. Experience working with multimodal or time-series data. Experience in a startup, deep-tech or early-stage product environment.
